summary: A roundtable recorded right after the August 2018 Unite the Right 2 white-nationalist rally in Washington, DC, debating whether physically confronting neo-Nazis works and criticising the police protection the marchers received.

evidence.note: Opening essay on Goebbels sending Berlin Nazis into leftist districts in Weimar Germany; comparison only
Nazi marchers arrive at Foggy Bottom metro station in DC and meet counter-protesters
Long discussion of police protecting the marchers and becoming the opposing force
Examples of police in Tennessee, Georgia and California siding with far-right activists
Optics and public sympathy as a battleground; media and propaganda theme
Segment reading and discussing Jason Kessler's post-rally tweets
Panel discusses white people's responsibility to confront white supremacy
Confrontation with a man filming a vulnerable protester to mock the counter-protest

notes: Bonus roundtable, recorded after a morning part one that is not in the feed. Hosts call the marchers Nazis throughout, so nazism is secondary; the Weimar Berlin material is a comparison and does not extend the covered span. Guest names come from on-air introductions with garbled transcript spellings (Lauren/Laurent Mario); Hannah co-hosts the Kitchen Table Cult podcast. Kessler's 1983 birth year is from general knowledge.
